hindi: अब इसके बाद हम 'तस्याशितीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called "Tasyāśitīya".
notes: Prose opening formula, not a verse (the unit is typed as "verse"). tasyāśitīya is a taddhita name formed from the opening words of verse 3, "tasyāśitād" (of him ... from what is eaten).

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, not a verse. sma with āha gives a past sense.

words.gloss: (from) what is eaten and the rest

hindi: जिसे चेष्टा और आहार पर आश्रित ऋतुसात्म्य ज्ञात है, उसके अशित आदि आहार से बल और वर्ण बढ़ता है।
english: The strength and complexion of him who knows the seasonal suitability (ṛtusātmya) that rests on conduct and diet increase from food eaten and the rest.
notes: aśitādyāt: "from eaten and the rest"; the ādi is not spelled out in the text. ca in line b joins the two predicates loosely; it is left untranslated. ṛtusātmya: what is suitable (wholesome by habituation) to each season.

hindi: यहाँ संवत्सर को ऋतु-विभाग से छह अंगों वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: Here one should know the year as having six parts by its division into seasons.
notes: Prose sentence, typed as a verse. khalu is an emphatic particle, left untranslated.

hindi: वहाँ सूर्य के उत्तरायण और आदान को शिशिर से आरम्भ होकर ग्रीष्म पर्यन्त तीन ऋतुएँ समझे, और फिर वर्षा से आरम्भ होकर हेमन्त पर्यन्त की ऋतुओं को दक्षिणायन और विसर्ग समझे।
english: Of these, one should determine the northward course of the sun and ādāna (taking up) to be the three seasons beginning with Śiśira and ending with Grīṣma; and, again, those beginning with Varṣā and ending with Hemanta to be the southward course and visarga (release).
notes: The six seasons in order: Śiśira, Vasanta, Grīṣma (ādāna, northward course); Varṣā, Śarad, Hemanta (visarga, southward course). "three" is stated only for the first group. Usual English equivalents (not words of the text): Śiśira late winter, Vasanta spring, Grīṣma summer, Varṣā rains, Śarad autumn, Hemanta early winter. ādāna and visarga: the periods in which the sun takes up and releases (moisture, strength), as the following units explain.
lines_deva: तत्रादित्यस्योदगयनमादानं च त्रीनृतूञ्छिशिरादीन् ग्रीष्मान्तान् व्यवस्येत् वर्षादीन् पुनर्हेमन्तान्तान् दक्षिणायनं विसर्गं च
lines_iast: tatrādityasyodagayanamādānaṃ ca trīnṛtūñchiśirādīn grīṣmāntān vyavasyet varṣādīn punarhemantāntān dakṣiṇāyanaṃ visargaṃ ca

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. caus. ā-√pṝ

hindi: विसर्ग में वायु अति रूक्ष नहीं बहते, किन्तु आदान में दूसरे बहते हैं; और अव्याहत बल वाला सोम शीतल किरणों से जगत् को भरता हुआ निरन्तर उसका आप्यायन करता है; इसलिए विसर्ग सौम्य है।
english: In visarga the winds blow not too dry; in ādāna, however, the others. And the moon, its strength unimpaired, filling the world with its cool rays, nourishes it continually; hence visarga is saumya (of the moon's nature).
notes: Prose, typed as a verse. "itare" (the others) are the winds that are very dry, with pravānti understood. vāyavaḥ here are physical winds, not the doṣa. āpūrayañ: āpūrayan before j.
lines_deva: विसर्गे पुनर्वायवो नातिरूक्षाः प्रवान्ति इतरे पुनरादाने सोमश्चाव्याहतबलः शिशिराभिर्भाभिरापूरयञ्जगदाप्याययति शश्वत् अतो विसर्गः सौम्यः
lines_iast: visarge punarvāyavo nātirūkṣāḥ pravānti itare punarādāne somaścāvyāhatabalaḥ śiśirābhirbhābhirāpūrayañjagadāpyāyayati śaśvat ato visargaḥ saumyaḥ

words.gloss: governed by time, nature and course
being causes of the production of time, season, taste, doṣa and bodily strength

hindi: आदान तो आग्नेय है। ये दोनों, सूर्य और वायु, तथा सोम, काल, स्वभाव और मार्ग से परिगृहीत होकर, काल, ऋतु, रस, दोष और देह-बल की निष्पत्ति के कारण बताए जाते हैं।
english: Ādāna, however, is āgneya (of fire's nature). These two, the sun and the wind, and the moon, governed by time, their own nature and their course, are taught to be the causes of the production of time, season, taste (rasa), doṣa and bodily strength.
notes: Prose, typed as a separate unit. vāyu here is the physical wind, not the doṣa Vāta. kālasvabhāvamārga may also be read as "the course natural to time" (a single idea); the split as three members is the more literal. deha-bala may be read as "body and strength" (two members); taken here as "bodily strength".
lines_deva: आदानं पुनराग्नेयं तावेतावर्कवायू सोमश्च कालस्वभावमार्गपरिगृहीताः कालर्तुरसदोषदेहबलनिर्वृत्तिप्रत्ययभूताः समुपदिश्यन्ते
lines_iast: ādānaṃ punarāgneyaṃ tāvetāvarkavāyū somaśca kālasvabhāvamārgaparigṛhītāḥ kālarturasadoṣadehabalanirvṛttipratyayabhūtāḥ samupadiśyante

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. ā-√dā
m. nom. pl. pres. part. caus. upa-√śuṣ
m. nom. pl. pres. part. caus. ut-√pad
m. nom. pl. pres. part. caus. abhi-√vṛdh

hindi: वहाँ सूर्य अपनी किरणों से जगत् के स्नेह को लेता हुआ, और तीव्र तथा रूक्ष वायु उसे सुखाते हुए, शिशिर, वसन्त और ग्रीष्म में क्रमशः रूक्षता उत्पन्न करते हुए और तिक्त, कषाय और कटु रूक्ष रसों को बढ़ाते हुए मनुष्यों में दुर्बलता लाते हैं।
english: There, the sun, taking up with its rays the moisture (sneha) of the world, and the winds, sharp and dry, drying it up, producing dryness in succession in Śiśira, Vasanta and Grīṣma and increasing the dry tastes, bitter, astringent and pungent, bring weakness to humans.
notes: Prose, typed as a verse. Finite verb āvahanti (pl.) has both the sun and the winds as subject. vāyavaḥ: physical winds. sneha here is the moisture/unctuousness of the world.
lines_deva: तत्र रविर्भाभिराददानो जगतः स्नेहं वायवस्तीव्ररूक्षाश्चोपशोषयन्तः शिशिरवसन्तग्रीष्मेषु यथाक्रमं रौक्ष्यमुत्पादयन्तो रूक्षान् रसांस्तिक्तकषायकटुकांश्चाभिवर्धयन्तो नृणां दौर्बल्यमावहन्ति
lines_iast: tatra ravirbhābhirādadāno jagataḥ snehaṃ vāyavastīvrarūkṣāścopaśoṣayantaḥ śiśiravasantagrīṣmeṣu yathākramaṃ raukṣyamutpādayanto rūkṣān rasāṃstiktakaṣāyakaṭukāṃścābhivardhayanto nṛṇāṃ daurbalyamāvahanti

words.gloss: whose heat is struck down by time, course, clouds, wind and rain
whose heat is calmed by the water of Mahendra

hindi: किन्तु वर्षा, शरद् और हेमन्त में, जब सूर्य दक्षिण की ओर मुख किए होता है और उसका प्रताप काल, मार्ग, मेघ, वायु और वर्षा से आहत होता है, चन्द्रमा अव्याहत बल वाला होता है, और जगत् का सन्ताप माहेन्द्र जल से शान्त हो जाता है, तब अम्ल, लवण और मधुर अरूक्ष रस क्रमशः बढ़ते हैं; तब मनुष्यों का बल बढ़ता है।
english: But in Varṣā, Śarad and Hemanta, when the sun faces the south and its heat is struck down by time, its course, clouds, wind and rain, when the moon is of unimpaired strength, and when the heat of the world is calmed by the water of Mahendra, the non-dry tastes, sour, salty and sweet, increase in succession; then the strength of humans grows.

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'mukjhe' (मुक्झे) is not a word; abhimukha 'facing' requires mukhe (मुखे).

notes: Prose, typed as a verse. māhendra salila, "the water of Mahendra" (Indra), means rain water; the identification is the usual one, not a word of the text. "jagati arūkṣā" is printed without sandhi (jagatyarūkṣā expected); not a reading difference. Final iti closes the prose statement and is not translated.
lines_deva: वर्षाशरद्धेमन्तेषु तु दक्षिणाभिमुक्झेऽर्के कालमार्गमेघवातवर्षाभिहतप्रतापे शशिनि चाव्याहतबले माहेन्द्रसलिलप्रशान्तसन्तापे जगति अरूक्षा रसाः प्रवर्धन्तेऽम्ललवणमधुरा यथाक्रमं तत्र बलमुपचीयते नृणामिति
lines_iast: varṣāśaraddhemanteṣu tu dakṣiṇābhimukjhe'rke kālamārgameghavātavarṣābhihatapratāpe śaśini cāvyāhatabale māhendrasalilapraśāntasantāpe jagati arūkṣā rasāḥ pravardhante'mlalavaṇamadhurā yathākramaṃ tatra balamupacīyate nṛṇāmiti

hindi: और यहाँ यह है: विसर्ग और आदान के आदि में और अन्त में मनुष्यों में दुर्बलता, मध्य में मध्यम बल, और अन्त में तथा आरम्भ में श्रेष्ठ बल बताना चाहिए।
english: And here there is: One should declare weakness of humans at the beginning and the end of visarga and ādāna, middling strength in the middle, and the best at the end and at the start.
notes: Line a is the lead-in formula "bhavati cātra" (and here there is [a verse]); "this" and "verse" are understood. The pairs are read in order (yathāsaṃkhya): weakness at the beginning of visarga and the end of ādāna; the best strength at the end of visarga and the start of ādāna. This reading is the usual one but the verse itself does not spell it out. śreṣṭham implies balam; the Hindi says "श्रेष्ठ बल".
lines_deva: मध्ये मध्यबलं त्वन्ते श्रेष्ठमग्रे च निर्दिशेत्
lines_iast: madhye madhyabalaṃ tvante śreṣṭhamagre ca nirdiśet

words.gloss: confined by the touch of cold wind
able to bear what is heavy in quantity and in substance

hindi: शीत हेमन्त में शीतल वायु के स्पर्श से अवरुद्ध पचाने वाला बलवानों में बलवान् होता है और मात्रा तथा द्रव्य से गुरु आहार को सहने में समर्थ होता है।
english: In the cold Hemanta, the digester, confined by the touch of cold wind, becomes strong in the strong, able to bear what is heavy in quantity and in substance.

text_flags.why: possible typing slip: the participle of saṃ-√rudh is saṃruddha with short u; metre is unaffected.

notes: paktā (the digester) is commonly taken as the digestive fire (agni); the text says only paktā. balināṃ balī: "strong in strong persons" (genitive in locative sense), or "strongest of the strong"; the first is followed here. mātrā-dravya-guru: food heavy by quantity and heavy by nature; "āhāra" is understood (the Hindi adds आहार for sense). anila here is the physical cold wind.

hindi: जब वह उचित इन्धन नहीं पाता, तब देह में उत्पन्न रस को हानि पहुँचाता है; इसलिए शीत वायु शीत में प्रकुपित होता है।
english: When it does not get suitable fuel, it then harms the body-born rasa; therefore Vāta (vāyu), being cold, is aggravated in the cold.
notes: rasa here is the body's rasa (the first dhātu), as dehaja "body-born" shows. vāyu is the doṣa, rendered Vāta per glossary. sa refers to paktā of unit 9.
lines_deva: स यदा नेन्धनं युक्तं लभते देहजं तदा
रसं हिनस्त्यतो वायुः शीतः शीते प्रकुप्यति
lines_iast: sa yadā nendhanaṃ yuktaṃ labhate dehajaṃ tadā
rasaṃ hinastyato vāyuḥ śītaḥ śīte prakupyati

words.gloss: of the meats of aquatic and marsh animals

hindi: इसलिए तुषार के समय में मेद वाले औदक और आनूप मांसों के स्निग्ध, अम्ल और लवण रसों का उपयोग करे।
english: Therefore, in the season of frost, one should use the unctuous, sour and salty rasas of the fat meats of aquatic and marsh animals.
notes: rasān with the genitive māṃsānām is read as "juices (meat soups) of meats"; it may also be read as two items: "unctuous, sour and salty tastes, and (the meats) of fat aquatic and marsh animals". Both are found; the English keeps "rasas". medya: fat, fleshy.

hindi: मनुष्य बिलेशयों के मांस और प्रसहों के भुने हुए मांस खाए, और उसके बाद मदिरा, शीधु और मधु पिए।
english: A man should eat the meats of burrow-dwellers and the roasted (meats) of prasaha animals, and drink after them madirā, śīdhu and madhu.
notes: prasaha: animals and birds that seize their prey (a class in Caraka's meat lists). bhṛta is taken as "roasted"; it may also mean "well cooked". madhu after madirā and śīdhu may be honey or a honey-wine; left as madhu. śīdhu is spelled sīdhu in unit 26; both spellings are found. "anu-" (after) is taken as "after eating"; the Hindi "उसके बाद" renders it.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. abhi-√as

hindi: हेमन्त में गोरस, इक्षु-विकार, वसा, तैल, नया ओदन और उष्ण जल का अभ्यास करने वाले की आयु क्षीण नहीं होती।
english: The life-span of one who regularly takes, in Hemanta, milk products, sugarcane preparations, muscle-fat (vasā), oil, new cooked rice and warm water does not diminish.
notes: navaudana: cooked rice of the new crop (nava "new").

hindi: अभ्यंग, उत्सादन, सिर पर तैल, जेन्ताक, धूप, तथा उष्ण भूमिगृह और उसी प्रकार उष्ण गर्भगृह का सेवन करे।
english: One should resort to oil massage (abhyaṅga), rubbing with unguents (utsādana), oil on the head, the jentāka (sweat-chamber), sunshine, and a warm underground house, and likewise a warm inner chamber.
notes: jentāka: a kind of sweating chamber, described in the chapter on sweating (svedādhyāya).

words.gloss: spread with cloaks, hides, silk, praveṇī and kuthaka

hindi: शीत ऋतुओं में ढका हुआ यान, शयन और आसन सेवनीय है, जो प्रावार, अजिन, कौशेय, प्रवेणी और कुथक से बिछा हो।
english: In the cold seasons, a covered vehicle, bed and seat should be used, spread with cloaks (prāvāra), hides (ajina), silk (kauṣeya), praveṇī and kuthaka.
notes: praveṇī and kuthaka are kinds of woven (woollen) coverings; their exact nature is not certain. ajina: hide, usually deerskin.

hindi: भारी और उष्ण वस्त्र पहने, सदा भारी अगुरु से लिप्त अंगों वाला, शय्या पर पीन तथा विशाल और भरे हुए स्तनों वाली प्रमदा को
english: Wearing heavy, warm clothes, his limbs always smeared with heavy aguru, in bed, a plump young woman with broad, full breasts
notes: The sentence continues into unit 17 (āliṅgya ... supyāt). aguru: aromatic wood; usually identified as Aquilaria agallocha (standard).

words.gloss: whose limbs are smeared with aguru
at the coming of the cold

hindi: आलिंगन करके, अगुरु से लिप्त अंगों वाली उसे, मद और काम से युक्त होकर सोए; और शिशिर के आगमन पर इच्छानुसार मैथुन का सेवन करे।
english: ...embracing her, whose limbs are smeared with aguru, he should sleep, full of intoxication and passion; and at the coming of the cold (śiśira) he should engage freely in sexual intercourse.
notes: Continues unit 16. śiśirāgame may mean "at the coming of the cold" (i.e. in Hemanta, the subject of these verses) or "at the coming of the Śiśira season"; both are possible. manmatha: passion, desire (also a name of the god of love; not taken as a name here).

words.gloss: at the coming of the cold

hindi: हिम के आगमन पर वातल और लघु अन्न-पान, प्रवात, प्रमित आहार और उदमन्थ का त्याग करे।
english: At the coming of the cold (hima) one should avoid foods and drinks that are Vāta-increasing and light, strong wind, a scanty diet, and udamantha.
notes: udamantha: roasted flour (of barley) stirred in water. pramita: measured, i.e. small in quantity.

words.gloss: born of clouds, wind and rain

hindi: हेमन्त और शिशिर समान हैं; शिशिर में थोड़ी विशेषता है: आदान से उत्पन्न रूक्षता, और मेघ, वायु तथा वर्षा से उत्पन्न शीत।
english: Hemanta and Śiśira are alike; in Śiśira there is a slight difference: dryness born of ādāna, and cold born of clouds, wind and rain.
notes: māruta here is the physical wind, not the doṣa.

hindi: इसलिए शिशिर में सम्पूर्ण हैमन्तिक विधि मानी जाती है; किन्तु शिशिर में निर्वात और अधिक उष्ण घर का आश्रय ले।
english: Therefore the whole regimen of Hemanta is prescribed in Śiśira; but in Śiśira one should resort to a house that is windless and warmer.
notes: adhikam may qualify uṣṇam ("more warm") or both adjectives ("more windless and warm"); the first is followed.

hindi: शिशिर में कटु, तिक्त और कषाय, वातल, लघु और शीतल अन्न-पान का त्याग करे।
english: In Śiśira one should avoid foods and drinks that are pungent, bitter and astringent, Vāta-increasing, light and cold.

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'varajayed' (वरजयेद्) has an extra a; the verb is varjayet (as in unit 18), and the extra syllable breaks the 8-syllable quarter.

words.gloss: by the rays of the day-maker

hindi: वसन्त में संचित श्लेष्मा दिनकृत् की किरणों से प्रेरित होकर कायाग्नि को बाधित करता है और तब अनेक रोग उत्पन्न करता है।
english: In Vasanta, the accumulated Kapha (śleṣman), stirred by the rays of the day-maker, impairs the digestive fire of the body (kāyāgni) and then produces many diseases.
notes: dinakṛt "day-maker" is an epithet of the sun. The text does not say where Kapha accumulated.

words.gloss: what is heavy, sour, unctuous and sweet

hindi: इसलिए वसन्त में वमन आदि कर्म कराए, और गुरु, अम्ल, स्निग्ध और मधुर का तथा दिवास्वप्न का त्याग करे।
english: Therefore in Vasanta one should have the procedures beginning with emesis (vamana) performed, and avoid what is heavy, sour, unctuous and sweet, and day-sleep.

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'kāreyet' (कारेयेत्) is not a form; the causative optative is kārayet. Syllable count is unaffected.

words.gloss: holding a mouthful moved in the mouth (kavalagraha)

hindi: कुसुमों के आगमन पर व्यायाम, उद्वर्तन, धूम, कवलग्रह, अञ्जन, और सुखद जल से शौच-विधि का अभ्यास करे।
english: At the coming of flowers one should practise exercise, rubbing (udvartana), medicated smoking (dhūma), holding a mouthful moved in the mouth (kavalagraha), collyrium (añjana), and the practice of cleansing with pleasant water.

text_flags.why: possible typing slip: the compound śauca-vidhi has short a (शौचविधिं); the long ā (शौचा-) gives no sense. Syllable count is unaffected.

notes: kusumāgama, "the coming of flowers", stands for Vasanta. sukhāmbu: water pleasant to the touch, usually taken as lukewarm.

words.gloss: with limbs smeared with sandal and aguru

hindi: चन्दन और अगुरु से लिप्त अंगों वाला, यव और गोधूम का भोजन करने वाला, शरभ, शश, एण, लाव और कपिञ्जल का मांस
english: With limbs smeared with sandal and aguru, eating barley and wheat, ... the meat of the śarabha, the hare, the eṇa deer, and of lāva and kapiñjala birds
notes: The sentence continues into unit 26 (bhakṣayet). Usual identifications (not words of the text): eṇa = black buck (probable), lāva = common quail (standard), kapiñjala = grey partridge (probable); śarabha is disputed (a large deer, or a fabulous animal). candana = sandalwood, Santalum album (standard); aguru = Aquilaria agallocha (standard).

hindi: ...खाए; हानिरहित सीधु या माध्वीक पिए; वसन्त में स्त्रियों और काननों के यौवन का अनुभव करे।
english: ...he should eat; he should drink harmless sīdhu, or just mādhvīka; in Vasanta he should enjoy the youth of women and of forests.
notes: Continues unit 25. nirgada "free of disease, harmless" is read with sīdhum. sīdhu is spelled śīdhu in unit 12. mādhvīka: a kind of wine; its base is not stated in the text.

hindi: ग्रीष्म में रवि अपनी किरणों से जगत् के स्नेह को बार-बार पीता है; तब मधुर, शीतल, द्रव और स्निग्ध अन्न-पान हितकर है।
english: In Grīṣma the sun drinks up again and again with its rays the moisture of the world; then food and drink that is sweet, cold, liquid and unctuous is wholesome.
lines_deva: स्वादु शीतं द्रवं स्निग्धमन्नपानं तदा हितम्
lines_iast: svādu śītaṃ dravaṃ snigdhamannapānaṃ tadā hitam

hindi: शर्करा सहित शीतल मन्थ, जांगल मृग और पक्षी, घृत, और शालि-अन्न सहित दूध का सेवन करता हुआ ग्रीष्म में कष्ट नहीं पाता।
english: Taking cold mantha with sugar, animals and birds of dry land (jāṅgala), ghee, and milk with śāli rice, one does not suffer in Grīṣma.
notes: mantha: roasted flour stirred in a liquid. saśālyannam may qualify payaḥ only ("milk with śāli rice") or stand as a separate item; read with payaḥ here. śāli: a class of rice.
lines_deva: घृतं पयः सशाल्यन्नं भजन् ग्रीष्मे न सीदति
lines_iast: ghṛtaṃ payaḥ saśālyannaṃ bhajan grīṣme na sīdati

words.gloss: salty, sour, pungent and hot things

hindi: मद्य थोड़ा पीना चाहिए, या नहीं पीना चाहिए, अथवा बहुत अधिक जल वाला पीना चाहिए; लवण, अम्ल, कटु और उष्ण पदार्थों तथा व्यायाम का त्याग करे।
english: Liquor should be drunk a little, or not at all, or else with very much water; one should avoid salty, sour, pungent and hot things, and exercise.

text_flags.why: typing slip: kaṭu 'pungent' has retroflex ṭ (कटू); the printed कतू gives no word. Metre is unaffected.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. pass. part. √sev

hindi: दिन में शीतल घर में निद्रा, और रात्रि में चन्द्र-किरणों से शीतल पदार्थों द्वारा सेवित होता हुआ, मोतियों और मणियों से विभूषित होकर आस्या का सेवन करे।
english: By day one should take sleep in a cool house; at night, attended by things cool with the moon's rays, adorned with pearls and gems, one should resort to sitting at rest (āsyā).

text_flags.suggest: (no reading suggested: line b repeats line b of unit 31 word for word)
text_flags.why: line b is word for word the same as line b of unit 31 and is probably repeated from it by error; with it, line a's śītalaiḥ has no noun. No other witness is in the input, so no replacement is offered.

notes: Translated as printed. "things" is supplied for the substantive adjective śītalaiḥ, which has no noun in the line. āsyā: sitting, a seat. See text_flags: line b is probably a repetition of 31b.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. pass. part. √sev

hindi: चन्दन-जल से शीतल पंखों और हाथों के स्पर्शों से सेवित होता हुआ, मोतियों और मणियों से विभूषित होकर आस्या का सेवन करे।
english: Attended with fans and touches of hands, cool with sandal-water, adorned with pearls and gems, one should resort to sitting at rest (āsyā).
notes: candanodakaśītalaiḥ qualifies both vyajanaiḥ and pāṇisaṃsparśaiḥ. āsyā: sitting, a seat.

hindi: ग्रीष्म काल में मैथुन से विरत मनुष्य शीतल कानन, जल और कुसुमों का सेवन करे।
english: In the season of Grīṣma a man, abstaining from sexual intercourse, should enjoy cool forests, waters and flowers.
lines_deva: काननानि च शीतानि जलानि कुसुमानि च
lines_iast: kānanāni ca śītāni jalāni kusumāni ca

hindi: आदान से दुर्बल देह में पचाने वाला दुर्बल हो जाता है; वह वर्षा में अनिल आदि के दूषणों से फिर बाधित होता है।
english: When the body is weakened by ādāna, the digester becomes weak; in the rains it is further impaired by the vitiations of Vāta (anila) and the others.
notes: paktā as in unit 9. anilādi: the doṣas, Vāta first.

words.gloss: from the vapour of the earth
from the downpour of the clouds

hindi: भूमि की भाप से, मेघों के बरसने से और जल के अम्ल पाक से, वर्षा में अग्नि-बल के क्षीण होने पर पवन आदि कुपित होते हैं।
english: From the vapour of the earth, the downpour of the clouds and the sour transformation (pāka) of water, in the rains, when the strength of the digestive fire (agni) is diminished, Vāta (pavana) and the others are aggravated.
notes: pākād amlāj jalasya: "from the sour pāka of water", i.e. water becoming sour in its transformation; amlāt may also be read as a separate cause ("from sourness"). pavanādi: the doṣas, Vāta first.

hindi: इसलिए वर्षा में सम्पूर्ण साधारण विधि प्रशस्त है। उदमन्थ, दिवास्वप्न, अवश्याय, नदी-जल,
english: Therefore in the rains the whole general regimen is commended. Udamantha, day-sleep, dew, river water,

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'sarsvo' (सर्स्वो) is not a word; sarvaḥ 'whole', as in unit 20 'sarvaḥ ... vidhiḥ'. The extra s does not change the syllable count.

notes: Line b continues into unit 36 (... varjayet). sādhāraṇa: general, common.

hindi: ...व्यायाम, आतप और व्यवाय का यहाँ त्याग करे; पान, भोजन और संस्कारों को प्रायः क्षौद्र से युक्त करके सेवन करे।
english: ...exercise, sunshine and sexual intercourse one should avoid here; one should take drinks, foods and preparations mostly mixed with honey (kṣaudra).
notes: Continues unit 35. pāna-bhojana-saṃskārān may also be read as "the preparations of drinks and foods" (tat-puruṣa).

words.gloss: with distinct sour, salt and fat

hindi: वर्षा में वात और वर्षा से आकुल, विशेष शीत वाले दिन, अनिल की शान्ति के लिए व्यक्त अम्ल, लवण और स्नेह वाला भोजन करना चाहिए।
english: In the rains, on a day troubled by wind and rain and especially cold, food with distinct sour, salt and fat should be eaten, for pacifying Vāta (anila).

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'vātārṣā' (वातार्षा) gives no word and leaves the half-line one syllable short (15); vāta-varṣa-ākula 'troubled by wind and rain' restores 16 syllables.
possible typing slip: anala 'fire' gives no sense (the fire is weak in the rains, unit 34, and should be protected, unit 38); anila 'Vāta' fits the sour, salty and unctuous food. Metre is unaffected.

notes: Translated with both corrections. If anala is kept, the line would read "for the calming of fire", which contradicts the context. "food" in the translation renders the neuter gerundive bhoktavyam (what is to be eaten). vāta in "wind and rain" is the physical wind.

words.gloss: by one intent on protecting the fire

hindi: अग्नि की रक्षा चाहने वाले को पुराने यव, गोधूम और शालि जांगल मांसों तथा संस्कृत यूषों के साथ खाने चाहिए।
english: By one intent on protecting the digestive fire (agni), old barley, wheat and śāli rice should be eaten with the meats of dry-land animals and with well-prepared soups (yūṣa).

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'jāṅgalaiar' (जाङ्गलैअर्) has an extra a; jāṅgalaiḥ māṃsaiḥ gives jāṅgalairmāṃsair. The extra vowel adds a syllable to the half-line.

notes: yūṣa: a soup, usually of pulses.

hindi: क्षौद्र से युक्त थोड़ा माध्वीक और अरिष्ट, अथवा जल पिए: उबालकर ठण्डा किया हुआ माहेन्द्र जल, या कूप का, या सरोवर का जल।
english: One should drink a little mādhvīka and ariṣṭa mixed with honey, or water: māhendra water boiled and cooled, or well water, or lake water.
notes: māhendra (water) "of Mahendra" means rain water; the identification is the usual one. ariṣṭa: a fermented medicinal preparation. mādhvīkāriṣṭam may also be read as "ariṣṭa made of mādhvīka".
lines_deva: माहेन्द्रं तप्तशीतं वा कौपं सारसमेव वा
lines_iast: māhendraṃ taptaśītaṃ vā kaupaṃ sārasameva vā

words.gloss: devoted to rubbing, anointing, bathing, perfumes and garlands
for the rainy season, of the rains

hindi: वह प्रघर्ष, उद्वर्तन, स्नान, गन्ध और माल्य में तत्पर रहे; लघु और शुद्ध वस्त्र पहनकर वर्षा ऋतु के योग्य क्लेद-रहित स्थान का सेवन करे।
english: One should be devoted to friction (pragharṣa), rubbing (udvartana), bathing, perfumes and garlands; wearing light, clean clothes, one should resort to a dwelling for the rainy season, free from dampness.

text_flags.why: typing slip: 'lagu' (लगु) for laghu 'light' (लघु); the aspirate is missing. Metre is unaffected.

notes: vārṣikam qualifies sthānam: "a dwelling of (for) the rainy season".

words.gloss: of those whose limbs are used to the cold of the rains

hindi: वर्षा के शीत के अभ्यस्त अंगों वाले और सहसा सूर्य की किरणों से तप्त हुए लोगों का संचित पित्त प्रायः शरद् में कुपित होता है।
english: In those whose limbs are used to the cold of the rains and who are suddenly heated by the sun's rays, the accumulated Pitta is generally aggravated in Śarad.
notes: eva with sahasā is a reinforcing particle; not rendered separately.

words.gloss: by those with keen desire (for food)

hindi: तब मधुर, लघु, शीतल, तिक्त से युक्त, पित्त को शान्त करने वाला अन्न-पान भली-भाँति आकांक्षा रखने वालों को मात्रा से सेवन करना चाहिए।
english: Then food and drink that is sweet, light, cold, with bitter, and pacifying Pitta, should be taken in due measure by those with keen desire for it.
notes: suprakāṅkṣitaiḥ: taken as "by those who have a keen desire (appetite)"; it may also qualify the time ("when well desired").

words.gloss: at the passing of the clouds

hindi: घनात्यय में लाव, कपिञ्जल, एण, उरभ्र, शरभ, शश, तथा यव और गोधूम सहित शालि सेवनीय कहे गए हैं।
english: At the passing of the clouds, they say, lāva and kapiñjala birds, eṇa deer, rams (urabhra), śarabhas, hares, and śāli rice with barley and wheat are to be taken.

text_flags.why: typing slip: urabhrān + śarabhān gives urabhrāñcharabhān; the printed 'chrabhān' (छ्रभान्) drops the a and leaves the half-line one syllable short (15).
typing slip: 'dhana' (wealth) gives no sense; ghanātyaya 'the passing of the clouds' (i.e. autumn) matches dhārādharātyaye in unit 44. Metre is unaffected.

notes: ghanātyaya, "the passing of the clouds", stands for Śarad. Animal identifications as in unit 25 (lāva standard, kapiñjala probable, eṇa probable, śarabha disputed); urabhra: ram, sheep.

words.gloss: at the passing of the rain-bearers

hindi: धाराधरों के अत्यय में तिक्त सर्पि का पान, विरेक, रक्तमोक्षण और आतप का वर्जन करना चाहिए।
english: At the passing of the rain-bearers, drinking of bitter ghee, purgation (vireka), blood-letting and avoidance of sunshine should be done.
notes: dhārādhara "bearer of torrents" = cloud; its passing stands for Śarad. tikta sarpis: bitter ghee.

hindi: यहाँ वसा, तैल, अवश्याय, औदक और आनूप आमिष, क्षार, दधि, दिवास्वप्न और पूर्व की वायु का त्याग करे।
english: Here one should avoid muscle-fat (vasā), oil, dew, the meat of aquatic and marsh animals, alkali (kṣāra), curd, day-sleep and the east wind.
notes: vāta in prāgvāta is the physical wind.
lines_deva: क्षारं दधि दिवास्वप्नं प्राग्वातं चात्र वर्जयेत्
lines_iast: kṣāraṃ dadhi divāsvapnaṃ prāgvātaṃ cātra varjayet

hindi: दिन में सूर्य की किरणों से सन्तप्त, रात्रि में चन्द्र की किरणों से शीतल, काल से पका हुआ, निर्दोष, अगस्त्य द्वारा निर्विष किया हुआ
english: Heated by the sun's rays by day, cooled by the moon's rays at night, matured by time, free of faults, made free of poison by Agastya,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 47 (haṃsodakam ... ambu). agastya: name; the line says only that Agastya made the water free of poison.

hindi: ...'हंसोदक' नाम से विख्यात, शारद, विमल और शुचि जल स्नान, पान और अवगाहन में अमृत के समान हितकर है।
english: ...the autumnal water, clear and pure, known as "haṃsodaka", is wholesome like amṛta for bathing, drinking and immersion.
notes: Continues unit 46. haṃsodaka: literally "swan-water".

hindi: शरद् काल में शारद माल्य और विमल वस्त्र प्रशस्त हैं, और प्रदोष में चन्द्रमा की किरणें।
english: In the season of Śarad, autumnal garlands and clean clothes are commended, and in the early night the rays of the moon.
notes: śāradāni mālyāni: garlands of autumn flowers.
lines_deva: शारदानि च माल्यानि वासांसि विमलानि च
lines_iast: śāradāni ca mālyāni vāsāṃsi vimalāni ca

hindi: इस प्रकार ऋतुसात्म्य कहा गया जो चेष्टा और आहार पर आश्रित है। जो अभ्यस्त होने से अनुकूल पड़ता है, वह ओकःसात्म्य कहलाता है।
english: Thus has been stated the seasonal suitability (ṛtusātmya) which rests on conduct and diet. What suits through habituation is called okaḥsātmya (suitability by habit).
notes: aucitya here means habituation, familiarity (from ucita "accustomed"), not propriety. okas: home, habit.

hindi: सात्म्य को जानने वाले देशों और रोगों के गुणों से विपरीत गुण वाली चेष्टा और आहार को भी सात्म्य मानते हैं।
english: Those who know suitability regard as suitable (sātmya) both conduct and food that are opposite in qualities to the qualities of regions and diseases.

text_flags.why: typing slip: sātmyajñāḥ + ceṣṭitam gives sātmyajñāśceṣṭitaṃ; the printed extra e (ज्ञाशेचे) adds a syllable to the half-line (17).

notes: "the qualities of" renders the instrumental guṇaiḥ with deśānām āmayānām (opposite to regions and diseases in their qualities). ādya: what is eaten, food.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक है: प्रत्येक ऋतु में मनुष्यों द्वारा जो कुछ सेवनीय और असेवनीय है, वह कारण सहित, और सात्म्य भी, तस्याशितीय में बताया गया है।
english: Here, the verse: Whatever is to be used and not to be used by humans in each season, with its reasons, and also suitability (sātmya), has been set out in the Tasyāśitīya.
notes: Line a is the lead-in "tatra ślokaḥ" (summary verse). ṛtāv ṛtau: repetition meaning "in each season".

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में तस्याशितीय नामक छठा अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Ślokasthāna of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the sixth chapter, named Tasyāśitīya.
notes: Chapter colophon. This edition names the section Ślokasthāna here (the chapter 1 colophon has sūtrasthāne); both names are used for the first section.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने तस्याशितीयो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne tasyāśitīyo nāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ
